summary: Owners with current selected-board access can archive one root from its row menu and restore it from the board Archive. store::transition_root changes only own state and the item and board revisions, committing them with an actor- and command-bound receipt. The board inventory includes group-inherited archive entries and distinguishes them from restorable roots.
evidence: Final serial browser_preview run: all 28 owned headless Chromium journeys passed (25 inherited, three new). An initial regression exposed a link with a layout box inside the collapsed recovery menu; explicitly hiding that link restored the read-only destination checks.

browser_archives_and_restores_one_root: Escape sent no write. While each command was pending the accepted state stayed visible. The grid excluded 67 after archive. Reloading the recovery address showed blocked 57 and restorable 67 without replay. Restore returned Ink 67 between 61 and 77, Active/3 at position 30, with board/3 and two receipts. A second board showed the empty Archive. Fresh connections compared the full stored rows, group metadata, board revisions and receipts, plus grants and session.

browser_recovers_failed_root_lifecycle: a deferred receipt error returned 500 and left the archive dialog and original database snapshot intact. Explicit Confirm reused the operation UUID. After a peer advanced the board revision, Restore returned 409 without a receipt; Reload recovery list issued only a GET. A new Restore used board/3 and item/2, committing board/4 and item/3. A stale archive was reviewed by the original UUID without another write.

browser_demoted_member_cannot_restore_root: demotion after listing caused one 403 and a fresh authorized inventory. Member and Viewer could inspect the list with disabled Restore and Archive; only Member had editable name controls. Withdrawing workspace membership showed Destination unavailable; rejecting the session returned to sign-in.

All 23 loopback_board_access cases passed. The new cases covered current session, grants and role including replay; foreign roots, invalid states and stale revisions; unchanged records after denied name/move/reorder/batch operations; one winner on competing host connections; command, actor and prior-receipt collisions; two migrations of populated v7 and account schemas with session and receipt preservation; Deleted ancestor precedence; a 100-row page of 102 and rejection of an unlisted restore; rollback of a restore exceeding the 500-row grid budget.

Locked workspace tests passed (38 tests, including the host suite), as did workspace fmt, git diff --check and host Clippy with browser-smoke tests. Builds used target-browser-packets. The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs before execution; those regressions remain for coordinator verification. Lost acknowledgments, failed post-commit refreshes and late lifecycle replies were not individually fault-injected in Chromium.
